title: The Restrainer and the Man of Lawlessness (Postmillennialism Today series)
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Reads 2 Thessalonians 2 as a first-century prophecy: the man of lawlessness is Nero, the restrainer is Claudius and Roman law (noting the claudere wordplay), and the temple is the Jerusalem temple.

title: Why a Gap in Daniel's 70 Weeks?
author: Thomas Ice
summary: Defends a gap between Daniel's 69th and 70th weeks on textual grounds (the events of 9:26 fall 'after the sixty-two weeks', not within the seventieth) and argues the gap view has early patristic precedent.

title: The Man of Sin, Part One (The Blessed Hope podcast on 2 Thessalonians 2:1-12)
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Amillennial treatment of 2 Thessalonians 2: an apostasy and the revelation of the man of sin must precede the Day of the Lord; weighs AD 70 against an end-of-age Antichrist.

title: The Man of Sin: Uncovering the Truth about the Antichrist
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Traces the Antichrist theme through Daniel, Jesus, Paul and John, arguing for both a recurring pattern of antichrists and a final end-time figure.

title: Isaiah 65:17-25: A Millennial Reign on Earth? Or a Vision of a New Heaven and Earth?
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: Argues Isaiah 65 depicts the consummated new creation in the idiom of the prophet's own day, with fulfilment beginning at Christ's first advent and completed at the final consummation.

title: The Millennium: Revelation 20:1-15
author: Sam Storms
summary: Amillennial exposition of Revelation 20 arguing the question is not literal versus spiritual but where the thousand years fit in John's recapitulating structure.

title: Postmillennialism in 1 Corinthians 15
author: Kenneth L. Gentry Jr.
summary: Argues from Paul's use of Psalm 110:1 that Christ reigns now and must subdue his enemies during the interadvental age, before the end and the resurrection.

title: Romans 11 and the Future of Ethnic Israel (JETS 43/4)
author: Benjamin L. Merkle
summary: Surveys the three main readings of 'all Israel' and argues for the total of elect Jews across history rather than a future mass conversion.

title: Daniel: The Key to Prophetic Revelation
author: John F. Walvoord
summary: Classic dispensational commentary: four empires ending in a revived Roman confederacy, a future Antichrist, and a gap before the seventieth week.

title: The Prophecy of Daniel: A Commentary
author: Edward J. Young
summary: Reformed, conservative commentary defending the sixth-century date, the Roman fourth kingdom and a messianic reading of Daniel 9:24-27.

title: The Gospel of Matthew (NICNT)
author: R. T. France
summary: Major commentary reading Matthew 24:4-35 as fulfilled in AD 70 (24:30 as Daniel 7:13 vindication) and 24:36 onward as the still-future parousia.

title: An Eschatology of Victory
author: J. Marcellus Kik
summary: Postmillennial exposition of Matthew 24 (dividing at 24:34-36) and Revelation 20.

title: Observations upon the Prophecies of Daniel, and the Apocalypse of St. John
author: Isaac Newton
summary: Historicist reading of Daniel: four empires, the ten kingdoms of divided Rome, the little horn as the papacy, and the seventy weeks dated from Artaxerxes.

title: Chronological Aspects of the Life of Christ
author: Harold W. Hoehner
summary: Calculates the sixty-nine weeks in 360-day prophetic years from Artaxerxes' decree to Nehemiah (444 BC) to the triumphal entry (AD 33).

title: The Climax of the Covenant: Christ and the Law in Pauline Theology
author: N. T. Wright
summary: Includes Wright's argument that 'all Israel' in Romans 11:26 is the whole people of God, Jew and Gentile together.

title: The Epistle to the Romans (NICNT)
author: Douglas J. Moo
summary: Major commentary holding that Romans 11:26 predicts a large-scale end-time conversion of ethnic Israel, at or near the parousia.

title: We Shall Meet Him in the Air: The Wedding of the King of Kings
author: Don K. Preston
summary: Full-preterist commentary on 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18, reading the parousia and gathering as fulfilled in the AD 70 consummation of the covenant.
note: Existence confirmed through bookseller listings; no stable publisher URL found.

title: The Cross and the Parousia of Christ: The Two Dimensions of One Age-Changing Eschaton
author: Max R. King
summary: King's major work presenting the resurrection of 1 Corinthians 15 as the corporate, covenantal raising of the body of Christ out of the old covenant, completed in AD 70.

title: He Will Reign Forever: A Biblical Theology of the Kingdom of God
author: Michael J. Vlach
summary: Dispensational biblical theology of the kingdom stressing a future earthly reign of Christ, including readings of Psalm 2, Psalm 110 and 1 Corinthians 15:20-28.

title: The End Times Made Simple
author: Samuel E. Waldron
summary: Short Reformed Baptist case for amillennialism built on the single general resurrection and judgment at Christ's one return.

title: 1 & 2 Thessalonians (Word Biblical Commentary)
author: F. F. Bruce
summary: Standard commentary surveying identifications of the restrainer (Roman order, the gospel mission, God, the Spirit) and the meaning of apantēsis.

title: The Church and the Tribulation
author: Robert H. Gundry
summary: Influential posttribulational argument, including the 'meeting' (apantēsis) of 1 Thessalonians 4:17 as an escort back to earth.

title: The Rapture Question (revised)
author: John F. Walvoord
summary: Standard pretribulational defense: the church is exempt from the day of wrath, and the restrainer of 2 Thessalonians 2 is the Spirit indwelling the church.

title: The Seventy Weeks and the Great Tribulation
author: Philip Mauro
summary: A former dispensationalist's argument that the seventy weeks run continuously and were fulfilled in Christ and the AD 70 judgment.

title: The Prophecy of Isaiah: An Introduction and Commentary
author: J. Alec Motyer
summary: Evangelical commentary on Isaiah treating 2:2-4, 9:6-7 and 65:17-25 as messianic and eschatological prophecy.

title: The Covenant of the Seventieth Week
author: Meredith G. Kline
summary: Argues that Messiah is the one who 'confirms the covenant' in Daniel 9:27 and that the seventieth week extends symbolically through the church age.
note: Published in The Law and the Prophets: Old Testament Studies in Honor of Oswald T. Allis (1974).
